title: ProjectE return_via_rules — per-netclass stitching thresholds, never one global number

local_return_via.$comment: Rule (1): the via connecting the entry and exit reference planes at a layer/reference change. Published thresholds span 1.27 mm (NXP i.MX 93) to 5.08 mm (TI TUSB564-Q1). Only 'closer is better' generalises.

edge_via_fence.$comment: Rule (2): plane-pair edge / RF region boundary. lambda/20 is a STARTING ESTIMATE, not a PASS/FAIL rule. No normative base standard exists.

threshold_source.$comment: A threshold without a source must emit NO_COVERAGE. Never universalise one number across net classes.

gssg_symmetry_required.$comment: Differential transitions need symmetric GSSG geometry relative to P/N, verified separately for mode conversion.

f_knee_edge_ghz.$comment: 0.35 / t_r. Derived from EDGE RATE, never from the clock frequency and never from f_nyquist.

frequency_basis.$comment: Only f_knee_edge is correct here. Any other basis is INVALID_METRIC for this rule.

lambda_divisor.$comment: 20 nominal, 10 as a loose upper bound.

labelled_as_estimate.$comment: This value must always be reported as an estimate, never as a PASS/FAIL rule.

escalation.$comment: If the region is critical, verify with 3D EM or measurement instead of trusting lambda/20.

$comment: dfm_emc_check.py --stitch-max-mm applies a single global threshold and therefore conflates these two different physics. Feed it per-netclass values from this file.
